newsitem.title: UK: BSkyB drops on soccer rights threat.
newsitem.headline: BSkyB drops on soccer rights threat.

text.p: Shares in British Sky Broadcasting Plc dropped in pre-market trade on Tuesday after a press report said soccer clubs were considering setting up their own television service when their deal with Sky expires in 2001.
BSkyB shares, already down 19 percent since June 12 -- partly due to the company being told to exit a group bidding for a digital television license -- were quoted down 14p at 472-1/2 by 0703 GMT.
Volume was a thin 2,640 shares at that point.

A report in the Financial Times said a consultants' report had advised the soccer Premier League that its 670 million stg, four-year deal with BSkyB represents only half the value of the television rights.
Analysts noted that sports coverage had been important in attracting subscribers to Sky cable and satellite services.

"Sport has been crucial for BSkyB," said Louise Barton, analyst at Henderson Crosthwaite. "This is only a recommendation, but if the Premier League goes along with it, the League with have control and they will dictate the terms...it is just another negative for BSkyB."

The FT said clubs were likely to react favourably to the recommendation from consultancy Oliver & Ohlbaum, since many were reported to be unhappy with how much money BSkyB is making from its soccer coverage.
No-one at Sky was immediately available for comment.

A further potential negative for the company was a report in the Times that Cable & Wireless Communications Plc and Telewest Communications Plc were in talks that could lead to a merger, increasing their ability to compete with BSkyB and British Telecommunications Plc.
By 0717 GMT BSkyB shares were down 31-1/2p at 455 in volume of 795,722 shares.
